objects.description: No structs, enums, typedefs, classes, or other user-defined types are defined in this header. It only defines a preprocessor macro OPENCENSUS_VERSION with a string literal value.

Thread-local operation context holding a TagMap and a Span. Conceptually immutable; manipulation is via API that produces new Context instances or temporarily sets the current one. Provides Current() to access the active thread-local Context, Wrap() to bind a callable to a snapshot of this context, and DebugString() for diagnostics. Construction details are private; default constructor and a mutable-current accessor are internal. Copyable and movable.

RAII-style scope guard that temporarily sets the current thread-local opencensus::context::Context to a provided value for the lifetime of the object. On construction, if cond is true, it swaps the current Context with an internal copy; on destruction it restores the original. It must be used on the same thread it is destroyed on. Copy/move and default construction are disabled. Details of Context are declared in opencensus/context/context.h and not part of this header.

TagMap is referenced but not defined in this header; its full definition resides elsewhere (opencensus/tags/tag_map.h). This header provides accessors that return const references to TagMap instances associated with a Context.

Context is referenced but not defined in this header; its full definition resides elsewhere (opencensus/context/context.h). This header uses Context only as an input to retrieve the associated TagMap.

Immutable, lightweight identifier type for a tag key used in OpenCensus tagging. TagKey values are registered via the static Register(name) factory and compare/hash by an internal 64-bit id. It is trivially destructible and thread-safe. The full implementation of Register() and name() is not present in this header.

Final class representing an immutable mapping from TagKey to string values with cached hash and equality semantics. Construction can be expensive; instances should be reused. Provides iterability via tags() (returns a const reference to an internal vector of sorted pairs), comparison operators, a debugging string, and a nested Hash functor compatible with unordered containers. Note: actual hashing and Initialize() implementation are not present in this header. Lifecycle: standard C++ object; no special destruction requirements beyond default destructor. Thread-safety not specified. Immutability holds after construction.
Nested functor usable as a hasher for TagMap in unordered containers. Applies a hash over a TagMap instance. Implementation is declared only here; details unspecified.

RAII-style scoped helper that, when constructed, conditionally installs the provided TagMap into the current thread-local OpenCensus context, and upon destruction restores the previous TagMap/context. If cond is false, it performs no change. It must be used and destroyed on the same thread. Copy/move are disallowed; intended for stack allocation. Details of Context/TagMap come from other headers.

Scoped enum (with underlying type uint8_t) of canonical Google RPC/HTTP-like status codes used by OpenCensus tracing to represent operation outcomes. Values include OK, CANCELLED, UNKNOWN, INVALID_ARGUMENT, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, NOT_FOUND, ALREADY_EXISTS, PERMISSION_DENIED, UNAUTHENTICATED, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, FAILED_PRECONDITION, ABORTED, OUT_OF_RANGE, UNIMPLEMENTED, INTERNAL, UNAVAILABLE, and DATA_LOSS. No constructors or owners; it is a plain enum for status reporting.

A small value-ref wrapper used by OpenCensus tracing to pass attribute values as a discriminated union of string, bool, or int64. It stores a Type tag and a union of absl::string_view, int64_t, or bool. For string values it holds a non-owning absl::string_view; the referenced storage must outlive the AttributeValueRef instance. It is copyable/movable and provides implicit constructors for strings, integral types (mapped to int64), and bool. Accessors require checking type() first. Equality compares both the type tag and contained value. DebugString provides a human-readable representation. No destructor or custom ownership semantics are defined; lifetime safety for string_view is the caller's responsibility.

objects.definition: enum class Type : uint8_t { kString, kBool, kInt };
objects.description: Strongly-typed discriminator indicating which value is stored in an AttributeValueRef: string, bool, or int64. Stored as an 8-bit enum class inside AttributeValueRef.

Abstract base class for span sampling policy. Implementations decide whether a span should be sampled based on context, IDs, name, and parent links. Thread-safe requirement is stated. Provides a single pure virtual ShouldSample method and virtual destructor.

Concrete Sampler implementing probabilistic sampling. Constructs with a probability (0.0–1.0) that is internally converted to a 64-bit threshold; sampling compares span randomness against this threshold. Thread-safe. Also has a private constructor taking a precomputed threshold and a friend TraceParamsImpl for global configuration.
Concrete Sampler that unconditionally samples every span. ShouldSample always returns true.
Concrete Sampler that never samples any span. ShouldSample always returns false.

objects.description: Forward declaration of Span. No definition is provided in this header; it is referenced as a pointer in Sampler interfaces. Details unknown here.

Final, immutable value-type representing an opaque 64-bit span identifier used to identify a span within a trace. Internally stores 8 bytes (kSize) and provides construction from a raw byte buffer, hex formatting, validity checking (non-zero), equality, and copying out the raw bytes. Details of byte ordering and validation beyond all-zeros are not specified in this header.

Final, immutable class representing a 128-bit trace identifier used to correlate spans within a trace. Stores 16 opaque bytes in rep_. Provides construction from a raw buffer, hex string formatting, equality comparison, validity check (non-zero bytes), access to raw value pointer, and copy-out to a caller-provided buffer. Details of endianness and formatting are not specified here.

Represents per-trace options propagated to child spans. Currently models a single byte of flags where at least one bit encodes whether the trace is sampled (IsSampled). Thread-compatible. Constructible with default (all options disabled) or from a raw kSize(=1)-byte buffer. Provides equality, hex formatting, copying to a buffer, and a method to return a modified copy with sampling set/unset. Details about which bit encodes sampling are not specified in this header.

Final, immutable value-type carrying tracing propagation state: TraceId, SpanId, and TraceOptions. Provides accessors, equality/inequality comparing only TraceId and SpanId, validity check, and string serialization. Construction is via default (all-zero/blank) or explicit TraceId/SpanId/(optional) TraceOptions. Copy/move operations are defaulted. Destruction and lifetime are automatic; no special ownership rules. Note: TraceId, SpanId, and TraceOptions are referenced types declared in other headers; details of their semantics are not defined here.

Final POD-like struct specifying limits for span data (attributes, annotations, message events, links) and the globally active sampling policy via a ProbabilitySampler. Used by TraceConfig to control tracing behavior. Field meanings inferred from names; no construction/destruction semantics beyond default are specified here.

Thread-safe configuration class in opencensus::trace that controls the currently active TraceParams used by tracing. Provides a single static mutator to update the global/active TraceParams; update is documented as non-atomic across individual fields. No instances are needed (or possible) for configuration changes since the API is static. Construction/destruction details are not applicable because the class exposes only static members and has no data defined here.
Span represents a tracing span. It is not defined in this header; only referenced via return type. No details are available here.
Context represents the execution context used by OpenCensus. It is only referenced as a parameter type in this header; no definition is present here.

Scoped RAII helper that conditionally makes a given opencensus::trace::Span the current span in the thread-local context for the lifetime of the object. On destruction, it restores the previous context; if constructed with end_span = true and the condition is true, it will call End() on the span when leaving scope. Must be used in the same thread where it is created. Copy/move operations are disabled; typically stack-allocated.

objects.description: Value-type class representing histogram bucket boundaries for distribution aggregations in OpenCensus stats. Provides factory methods for linear, exponential, and explicit boundary configurations; exposes the number of buckets, boundary access, bucket lookup for a value, and debug string. Thread-compatible. Construction is via the provided static factory methods; the only constructor is private. Destruction is standard value-type semantics; no special ownership requirements beyond typical C++ object lifetime. Exact validation rules and error handling for invalid inputs are not specified in this header.

Immutable configuration object describing how a metric/view should aggregate recorded measurements. It supports Count, Sum, Distribution (with histogram bucket boundaries), and LastValue modes. Constructed via its static factory methods; copyable and comparable. DebugString() provides a textual form. bucket_boundaries_ is only meaningful when type() == Type::kDistribution.
Scoped enumeration inside Aggregation indicating which aggregation behavior is selected: count of records, sum of values, distribution (histogram/statistics), or last recorded value.

Final class summarizing a stream of double values with histogram buckets and basic statistics (count, mean, variance via sum of squared deviation, min, max). It references BucketBoundaries (not owned) to define bucket layout. Construction and mutation are private; intended to be populated by friend classes (e.g., ViewDataImpl, MeasureData, testing::TestUtils). Thread-compatible per comments.

objects.description: Alias for Measure<double>, representing a floating-point measure that accepts double-valued recordings.

objects.definition: typedef Measure<int64_t> MeasureInt64;
objects.description: Alias for Measure<int64_t>, representing an integral measure that accepts 64-bit integer recordings.

Immutable pairing of a Measure (double or int64) and a corresponding value to record. It stores the associated measure id and the typed value in a union. Constructible only with a matching MeasureDouble/MeasureInt64 and a value whose type category matches (floating-point for double, integral for int64). Used internally by the stats system to record events.

Immutable metadata class describing a stats Measure in OpenCensus. Holds the measure's name, human-readable description, units, and value type. Instances are constructed internally (by MeasureRegistryImpl) and expose read-only accessors plus comparison and a DebugString method. Construction is restricted; users should obtain instances via MeasureRegistry::Register* APIs (not defined here).

Strongly-typed scoped enumeration nested in MeasureDescriptor indicating the value type recorded by the associated Measure: double or int64. As a scoped enum class, it does not implicitly convert to integers.

Thread-safe registry class that tracks all MeasureDescriptors registered in the process and allows querying by measure name. Provides static lookup functions that return a descriptor by name or a typed Measure (double or int64). The class is final and only exposes static methods; no instances are expected to be constructed by users.

RAII handle in opencensus::stats that starts and stops on-task data collection for a ViewDescriptor. Constructing a View begins collection (if the underlying measure is registered). The object is non-copyable and thread-safe. Destruction stops collection. GetData retrieves a snapshot (copy) of current ViewData. Validity can be checked via IsValid. Internally holds a const copy of the ViewDescriptor and an opaque StatsManager::ViewInformation handle pointer. Details of construction success and data semantics depend on the referenced measure and StatsManager internals, which are not defined here.

Final value-type class that describes an OpenCensus stats View: its unique name, target measure, aggregation, tag-key columns, optional description, expiry, and aggregation window. It supports builder-style setters, equality, debug string, and registration for export. Construction details: default constructs with cumulative aggregation; measure must reference a registered MeasureDescriptor by name; registration requires cumulative window. Thread-compatible; owners typically pass by value. Unknowns: exact semantics of aggregation_window_ mutation are internal; lifetime/ownership of referenced measure and tag keys are external.

Immutable snapshot of aggregated statistics for a specific View. It exposes the aggregation type and provides read-only access to per-tag-value data maps, which are keyed by vectors of tag values and hold either double, int64, or Distribution values depending on the view's Aggregation. It also provides time bounds (start times per key and an overall end time). Construction is private; instances are produced by the library internals (e.g., View) and are copyable but not mutable. Destruction is automatic; it owns an internal implementation via unique_ptr.
Scoped enumeration inside ViewData indicating which value map is valid for this snapshot: double, int64, or Distribution.

Thread-safe manager for stats export. It coordinates registration of push handlers and exposes pull APIs for retrieving current View data. Provides static lifecycle/control methods only; instances are not constructible. The nested Handler interface defines the callback for push exporters. Details like storage, threading model, and handler ownership are internal and not exposed here.

Abstract interface for push exporters used by StatsExporter. Implementations receive periodic callbacks with current ViewDescriptor/ViewData pairs via ExportViewData. Instances are registered using StatsExporter::RegisterPushHandler and are owned by the exporter subsystem after registration.

functions.name: opencensus::context::Context::Current
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the thread-local current Context. Use this to read the active operation context (e.g., tags and span) for the calling thread. The reference is non-owning and read-only; mutate the context by constructing a new Context via the public API that changes context (not shown here) rather than modifying in-place.
requirements: May be called from any thread; returns that thread’s current Context.
The returned reference is const; callers must not attempt to modify the Context.
The returned reference is non-owning; do not assume it outlives changes to the thread-local current Context (avoid storing it beyond immediate use).
Thread-local behavior is implied: the value refers to the calling thread’s current Context.

functions.name: opencensus::context::Context::Wrap
functions.description: Returns a new callable that, when invoked, executes the provided function fn with a copy of this Context active. Useful for capturing the current Context and propagating it into deferred work (e.g., callbacks, task queues). The wrapping does not change fn itself; it arranges that fn runs under this Context’s snapshot.
requirements: fn must be a valid std::function<void()>; passing an empty function object leads to undefined behavior on invocation (inferred from std::function semantics).
The returned callable does not guarantee any specific threading behavior; callers must arrange safe execution contexts if used across threads (details not specified in this header).
Any exceptions thrown by fn will propagate to the caller of the returned callable (not specified here; default C++ behavior).

functions.name: opencensus::context::Context::DebugString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string representation of the Context intended for debugging. The format is unspecified and may change; do not parse or depend on its contents to retrieve spans or tags.
requirements: The returned string is for debugging only; callers must not parse it or rely on its format.
Do not use this output to retrieve Spans or Tags; use the public API for that instead.

functions.name: opencensus::context::WithContext::WithContext
functions.description: Constructs a scoped RAII guard that, if cond is true, makes the provided Context the current thread-local Context for the lifetime of this WithContext object, restoring the previous Context when the guard is destroyed. If cond is false, construction succeeds but the current Context is left unchanged. Typical usage is stack allocation to temporarily run code under a specific Context.
requirements: Must be constructed and destroyed on the same thread; do not allocate in one thread and deallocate in another (because it manipulates a thread-local current Context).
The ctx argument must refer to a valid, initialized opencensus::context::Context at the time of construction.
This type is not copyable or movable; callers must not attempt to copy or move a WithContext instance.
A WithContext instance should remain alive for the entire duration during which the temporary Context should be active; upon destruction the previous Context is restored.
Effects are limited to the current thread’s thread-local Context.

functions.name: opencensus::context::WithContext::~WithContext
functions.description: Destructs the WithContext guard, restoring the previously active thread-local Context if the guard had changed it during construction (i.e., when cond was true). If construction did not change the Context (cond was false), destruction is a no-op with respect to the current Context.
requirements: Must be destroyed on the same thread where the WithContext object was constructed; do not deallocate on a different thread.
Destruction should occur after all operations that rely on the temporary Context have completed, so the restoration does not interfere with ongoing work.

functions.description: Returns the TagMap associated with the current Context. Typical usage is to read the current set of tags (key/value pairs) that are bound to the active context (often thread-local). The function exposes the TagMap as a const reference; use it for inspection, not modification. The exact lifetime of the returned reference depends on the lifetime of the current Context; details are not documented in this header and are inferred.
requirements: Caller must treat the returned TagMap as read-only (it is returned as a const reference).
Caller must not store the returned reference beyond the lifetime/scope of the current Context (inferred from returning a reference to context-owned data; exact lifetime details are not documented).
Function must be called when a current Context is established; behavior with no active Context is not documented (unknown).

functions.description: Returns the TagMap contained in the provided Context. Use this to inspect the tags for a specific Context instance rather than the implicitly current one. The TagMap is returned as a const reference; it is intended for read-only access. The reference’s validity is tied to the provided Context’s lifetime; details are not documented in this header and are inferred.
requirements: The ctx parameter must refer to a valid opencensus::context::Context object.
Caller must treat the returned TagMap as read-only (it is returned as a const reference).
Caller must not store the returned reference beyond the lifetime of the provided Context (inferred from returning a reference to context-owned data; exact lifetime details are not documented).

functions.description: Registers (or looks up) a tag key by name and returns a lightweight, immutable TagKey handle. Re-registering the same name yields an equal TagKey. Typical usage: call once per logical tag key and reuse the returned TagKey for tagging operations.
requirements: name: no explicit constraints stated in this header (length/contents unknown).
Equal TagKeys are produced when the same name is registered multiple times (identity defined by name).
Thread-safety: TagKey is documented as thread-safe; concurrent calls are expected to be safe (no stricter requirement stated).

The returned string is immutable via this interface (const reference).

functions.name: opencensus::stats::Record
functions.description: Records a list of stats Measurements under the current Context's tags. Use an initializer list to pass multiple measurements, e.g., Record({{measure_double, 2.5}, {measure_int, 1ll}}). Only floating-point values may be recorded against MeasureDoubles and only integral values against MeasureInt64s to avoid precision loss; mismatched types will fail to compile. Intended for recording point-in-time metric values associated with the process’s current tag context.
requirements: Each Measurement must pair a MeasureDouble with a floating-point value or a MeasureInt64 with an integral value; use static_cast<double> or static_cast<int64_t> if needed.
The measurements parameter must be a valid initializer_list of Measurement objects.
Recording uses the current Context's tags; callers should ensure the desired tag context is active before calling if tag attribution matters.
No return value is provided; callers should not expect exceptions or error indicators from this API (error behavior unspecified in header).

functions.name: opencensus::stats::Record
functions.description: Records a list of stats Measurements using the provided TagMap, ignoring the current Context's tags. Use an initializer list for measurements and supply explicit tags, e.g., Record({{measure_double, 2.5}}, {{key, "value"}}). Type safety is enforced: MeasureDoubles accept only floating-point values and MeasureInt64s accept only integral values; mismatches will fail to compile.
requirements: Each Measurement must pair a MeasureDouble with a floating-point value or a MeasureInt64 with an integral value; use static_cast<double> or static_cast<int64_t> if needed.
The measurements parameter must be a valid initializer_list of Measurement objects.
The tags argument must be a valid opencensus::tags::TagMap specifying the tags to associate with the recorded measurements; the current Context's tags are ignored when this overload is used.
No return value is provided; callers should not expect exceptions or error indicators from this API (error behavior unspecified in header).

import struct
import string

# Target expects arbitrary strings used as std::string/absl::string_view inputs.
# We generate a single bytes buffer without embedding Python source null bytes
# in string literals of this script; all nulls are produced at runtime.
# The buffer aggregates length-prefixed segments suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# slicing and fixed-size byte needs (TraceId=16, SpanId=8, TraceOptions=1).

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_bytes(rng, n):
    # Mix of printable, utf-8 multibyte, and binary
    chunks = []
    total = 0
    while total < n:
        choice = rng.randrange(5)
        if choice == 0:
            # printable ascii
            l = min(n - total, rng.randint(4, 32))
            s = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.//:") for _ in range(l))
            chunks.append(s.encode('ascii'))
        elif choice == 1:
            # utf-8 words
            words = ["alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "日本語", "😀", "🚀", "naïve", "ümlaut"]
            w = rng.choice(words).encode('utf-8')
            chunks.append(w)
        elif choice == 2:
            # zero bytes (produced at runtime)
            l = min(n - total, rng.randint(1, 16))
            chunks.append(bytes([0]) * l)
        elif choice == 3:
            # structured little-endian integers
            val = rng.getrandbits(64)
            chunks.append(struct.pack('<Q', val))
        else:
            # random binary
            l = min(n - total, rng.randint(8, 64))
            chunks.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(l)))
        total = sum(len(c) for c in chunks)
    out = b''.join(chunks)
    if len(out) > n:
        out = out[:n]
    return out

def _make_fixed(rng, size, fill=None):
    if fill is None:
        return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))
    if isinstance(fill, int):
        return bytes([fill]) * size
    return bytes(fill[:size]).ljust(size, b'\x00')

def _make_length_prefixed(payload):
    # 32-bit little-endian length prefix
    return struct.pack('<I', len(payload)) + payload

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    blobs = []

        b = text.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

        "root-span", "child/span", "rpc.client", "rpc.server", "db.query",
        "io.read", "io.write", "compute", "startup", "shutdown"
    ]
    messages = [
        "OK", "Cancelled", "Invalid argument", "Deadline exceeded",
        "Not found", "Already exists", "Permission denied", "Unauthenticated",
        "Internal error", "Data loss"
    ]
    keys = [
        "http.method", "http.path", "user.id", "retry", "size", "success",

    ]

    blobs.append(_make_length_prefixed(_make_fixed(rng, 16, fill=0xFF)))
    blobs.append(_make_length_prefixed(_make_fixed(rng, 16)))

    blobs.append(_make_length_prefixed(_make_fixed(rng, 8, fill=0xFF)))
    blobs.append(_make_length_prefixed(_make_fixed(rng, 8)))

    blobs.append(_make_length_prefixed(_rand_bytes(rng, arena_len)))

    out = b''.join(blobs)
    return out[:MAX_TOTAL]

    for _ in range(8):
        ints.append(rng.randint(-2**63+1, 2**63-2))
    rng.shuffle(ints)
    for iv in ints:
        buf += _pack_i64(iv)

    # Emit strings likely to be used as keys and values. Limit to 1024 for values.
    strings = [
        b"", b"a", b"key", b"value", b"true", b"false", b"0", b"1",
        _rand_ascii(rng, 5, 20),
        _rand_utf8ish(rng, 10, 40),
        _rand_ascii(rng, 100, 200),
        _rand_utf8ish(rng, 500, 800)
    ]
    rng.shuffle(strings)
    for s in strings:
        # Cap at 1024 to satisfy fuzzer stub resize
        if len(s) > 1024:
            s = s[:1024]
        _emit_string(rng, buf, s)
        # Separate strings with a zero byte to help parsers that look for C-strings
        buf += b"\x00"

    # Include a few key/value pairs for Span::AddAttribute
    for _ in range(6):
        # key
        key = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 16)
        _emit_string(rng, buf, key + b"\x00")
        # choice for attribute type
        buf += _pack_u32(rng.randrange(0, 3))
        t = rng.randrange(0, 3)
        if t == 0:
            val = _rand_utf8ish(rng, 0, 64)
            _emit_string(rng, buf, val + b"\x00")
        elif t == 1:
            buf += _pack_i64(rng.randint(-2**63+1, 2**63-2))
        else:
            buf += _pack_u32(rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 0xFFFFFFFF]))

    # Ensure we stay within the 4096 byte limit.
    return bytes(buf[:MAX_BUF])

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzzing stubs that consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR and int64_t.
# It builds a structured buffer containing diverse integers and a table of
# length-prefixed strings. Kept <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

KEY_LIKE_STRINGS = [
    "key", "k", "attr", "flag", "count", "id", "user_id", "session",
    "trace", "span", "status", "ok", "error", "true", "false",
    "http.method", "http.status_code", "db.statement", "component",
]

VALUE_LIKE_STRINGS = [
    "", "0", "1", "true", "false", "on", "off", "enabled", "disabled",
    "GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH",
    "200", "201", "400", "401", "403", "404", "409", "429", "500", "503",
    "sqlite", "select * from t", '{"": "v"}', "name", "value",
]

UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "αβγ", "日本語", "emoji😊", "🌐🌟", "русский", "árvíztűrő tükörfúrógép",
]


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.//:"
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_utf8_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII and random UTF-8 code points.
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        mode = r.randint(0, 9)
        if mode < 6:
            out.append(r.randint(32, 126))  # ASCII printable
        elif mode < 8:
            ch = 0x00C0 + r.randint(0, 0x3FF)
            out += chr(ch).encode('utf-8')
        else:
            ch = 0x0800 + r.randint(0, 0x7FF)
            out += chr(ch).encode('utf-8')
    return bytes(out[:n])


def _pack_i64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<q', x)


def _pack_u64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<Q', x & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)


def _len_prefixed(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # 32-bit little endian length prefix
    return struct.pack('<I', len(b)) + b


def _build_strings(r: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Deterministic set of useful strings
    base_strings: List[str] = []
    base_strings += KEY_LIKE_STRINGS
    base_strings += VALUE_LIKE_STRINGS
    base_strings += UNICODE_SNIPPETS
    # Add random sized ASCII
    for _ in range(5):
        base_strings.append(_rand_ascii(r, r.randint(1, 32)))
    # Add longer strings (including ~1KB to match stub cap)
    long_len = r.choice([64, 128, 256, 512, 1024])
    base_strings.append(_rand_ascii(r, long_len))
    # Add UTF-8 random
    base_strings.append(_rand_utf8_bytes(r, r.randint(5, 40)).decode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # Shuffle for variety
    r.shuffle(base_strings)

    total = 0
    for s in base_strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        chunk = _len_prefixed(b)
        if total + len(chunk) > budget:
            break
        parts.append(chunk)
        total += len(chunk)
    return b"".join(parts)


def _build_integers(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    ints: List[int] = []
    # Boundary and interesting values
    ints += [0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3]
    ints += [2**63 - 1, -2**63, 2**31 - 1, -2**31]
    # Some powers of two and masks
    for k in [8, 16, 32, 40, 48, 56]:
        ints.append(1 << (k - 1))
        ints.append(-(1 << (k - 1)))
        ints.append((1 << k) - 1)
    # Random ints
    for _ in range(16):
        # Uniform over 64-bit signed range
        val = r.getrandbits(64)
        if val >= (1 << 63):
            val -= (1 << 64)
        ints.append(val)
    # Mix in alternating patterns for LSB variety (booleans)
    pattern = 0
    for _ in range(16):
        pattern ^= 1
        ints.append(pattern)
    # Pack as little-endian i64
    buf = bytearray()
    for x in ints:
        buf += _pack_i64(int(x))
    return bytes(buf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Layout:
    # [magic][version]
    # [count_u64][u64 array]
    # [count_i64][i64 array]
    # [string_table_size][string_table bytes (len-prefixed strings)]

    magic = b"OCEN"
    version = struct.pack('<I', 1)

    # Unsigned 64s for general entropy consumers
    u64_vals = [
        0, 1, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA, 0x5555555555555555,
        0x0123456789ABCDEF, 0xFEDCBA9876543210,
    ]
    u64_vals += [r.getrandbits(64) for _ in range(16)]
    u64_blob = b''.join(_pack_u64(x) for x in u64_vals)
    u64_hdr = struct.pack('<I', len(u64_vals))

    # Signed 64s to satisfy int64_t requests
    i64_blob = _build_integers(r)
    i64_count = struct.pack('<I', len(i64_blob) // 8)

    # Strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR: allocate about half of remaining budget
    fixed = len(magic) + len(version) + len(u64_hdr) + len(u64_blob) + len(i64_count) + len(i64_blob) + 4
    budget = max(0, MAX_TOTAL - fixed)
    str_table = _build_strings(r, max(128, budget // 2))
    str_size = struct.pack('<I', len(str_table))

    buf = bytearray()
    buf += magic
    buf += version
    buf += u64_hdr
    buf += u64_blob
    buf += i64_count
    buf += i64_blob
    buf += str_size
    buf += str_table

    return bytes(buf[:MAX_TOTAL])

import random
import struct
import os

# Target data type: fixed-length 8-byte binary (opaque). Used by stubs to build SpanId (kSize=8),
# but the fuzzer also consumes other sized buffers and strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and other sizes.
# Our generator should return an initial seed buffer that the fuzzer framework slices into pieces
# for FUZZ_PARAM(uint8_t[16]), FUZZ_PARAM(uint8_t[8]), FUZZ_PARAM_STR, etc.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a compact container format that concatenates several well-formed segments in this order:
#   [trace_id 16][span_id 8][parent_trace_id 16][parent_span_id 8][trace_options 1]
#   [alt_trace_id 16][alt_span_id 8][alt_opts 1]
#   [name strings blob with lengths]
#   [extra entropy padding]
# - We include multiple trace/span IDs to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM() pulls across stubs.
# - Ensure non-zero IDs frequently to pass IsValid() checks in link-related stubs, but also allow
#   occasional zero IDs to exercise invalid paths.
# - Provide several interesting name strings to exercise sampler name handling.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Note: We do not apply mutational fuzzing post-generation; we generate valid-looking bytes.

_DEF_NAMES = [
    "get:/api/v1/resource",
    "post:/items",
    "WorkerTask#run",
    "grpc:MyService.Method",
    "",
    "unicode-π-測試",
    "VeryLongOperationName/" + ("x" * 120),
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int, nonzero_bias: float = 0.8) -> bytes:
    # Generate bytes with bias toward non-zero to get valid IDs; still include zeros sometimes.
    out = bytearray(n)
    for i in range(n):
        if rng.random() < nonzero_bias:
            out[i] = rng.randrange(1, 256)
        else:
            out[i] = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    return bytes(out)


def _make_trace_id(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 16 bytes; ensure not all-zero most of the time.
    for _ in range(5):
        b = _rand_bytes(rng, 16, nonzero_bias=0.9)
        if any(b):
            return b
    return b  # fallback


def _make_span_id(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 8 bytes; ensure not all-zero most of the time.
    for _ in range(5):
        b = _rand_bytes(rng, 8, nonzero_bias=0.9)
        if any(b):
            return b
    return b


def _make_trace_opts(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 1 byte; bit 0 as sampled toggled with some probability.
    sampled = 1 if rng.random() < 0.6 else 0
    other_bits = rng.randrange(0, 256) & 0xFE
    return bytes([(other_bits | sampled) & 0xFF])


def _encode_len_prefixed_strings(strings: list[str]) -> bytes:
    # Format: u16 count, then for each: u16 byte-length, bytes (UTF-8)
    # Keep lengths bounded to avoid huge buffers.
    parts = []
    count = min(len(strings), 255)
    parts.append(struct.pack("<H", count))
    for s in strings[:count]:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')
        if len(b) > 512:
            b = b[:512]
        parts.append(struct.pack("<H", len(b)))
        parts.append(b)
    return b"".join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Core IDs used by multiple stubs
    trace_id = _make_trace_id(rng)
    span_id = _make_span_id(rng)
    p_trace_id = _make_trace_id(rng)
    p_span_id = _make_span_id(rng)
    opts = _make_trace_opts(rng)

    # Additional contexts for other calls
    alt_trace_id = _make_trace_id(rng)
    alt_span_id = _make_span_id(rng)
    alt_opts = _make_trace_opts(rng)

    # Build a pool of names mixing defaults with random components
    names = list(_DEF_NAMES)
    # Add a couple of seeded-random names
    verbs = ["GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH"]
    resources = ["/", "/health", "/login", "/users/123", "/search?q=abc"]
    svc = ["Auth", "Catalog", "Billing", "Orders"]
    meth = ["List", "Get", "Create", "Update", "Delete"]
    for _ in range(3):
        names.append(f"{rng.choice(verbs)} {rng.choice(resources)}")
        names.append(f"rpc://{rng.choice(svc)}.{rng.choice(meth)}")
    # Deduplicate while keeping order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for s in names:
        if s not in seen:
            uniq.append(s)
            seen.add(s)
    names_blob = _encode_len_prefixed_strings(uniq)

    # Extra entropy to satisfy additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls and byte arrays.
    extra = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(64, 256), nonzero_bias=0.7)

    # Assemble buffer
    parts = [
        trace_id,            # 16
        span_id,             # 8
        p_trace_id,          # 16
        p_span_id,           # 8
        opts,                # 1
        alt_trace_id,        # 16
        alt_span_id,         # 8
        alt_opts,            # 1
        names_blob,          # variable
        extra,               # variable
    ]
    buf = b"".join(parts)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return buf

from typing import List

# Target data type: fixed-length 1-byte binary
# Used by fuzzers for opencensus::trace::TraceOptions construction where kSize == 1.
# Our goal: generate interesting yet valid single-byte buffers that exercise
# different TraceOptions states (e.g., sampled bit on/off and other flag patterns)
# while remaining exactly 1 byte long.

_INTERESTING_BYTES: List[int] = [
    0x00,  # all bits cleared (unsampled)
    0x01,  # only LSB set (commonly sampled bit)
    0xFF,  # all bits set
    0x80,  # high bit set
    0x7F,  # all but high bit set
    0x55,  # 01010101 pattern
    0xAA,  # 10101010 pattern
    0x0F,  # low nibble set
    0xF0,  # high nibble set
    0x03,  # two LSBs set
]

def _rand_byte(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias towards interesting values while allowing full 0-255 coverage.
    if rng.random() < 0.75:
        return rng.choice(_INTERESTING_BYTES)
    return rng.randrange(0, 256)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    b = _rand_byte(rng)
    return bytes([b])
